restated_task: Implement the to_roman(n) function in the roman.core module to convert an integer n in the range 1..3999 inclusive to its standard Roman numeral string using subtractive notation (e.g., 4='IV', 9='IX', 40='XL', 90='XC', 400='CD', 900='CM'). The function must return a string. It must raise ValueError for integer inputs outside the valid range and TypeError for non-integer inputs (including bool, since only real ints are valid). The existing is_roman_numeral function and the test suite must remain unchanged.

interface_contract.name: is_roman_numeral
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True if s is a non-empty string consisting only of Roman numeral letters (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) case-insensitively; otherwise returns False. This function is already implemented and must not be modified.

interface_contract.name: to_roman
interface_contract.behavior: Converts an integer n in the range 1..3999 inclusive to its standard Roman numeral representation using subtractive notation. The mapping uses the following value-symbol pairs in descending order: 1000='M', 900='CM', 500='D', 400='CD', 100='C', 90='XC', 50='L', 40='XL', 10='X', 9='IX', 5='V', 4='IV', 1='I'. The function returns the resulting string.
error_cases: ValueError: raised when n is an integer but not in the range 1..3999 (e.g., 0, -1, 4000).
TypeError: raised when n is not an integer (e.g., string, float, None, list). Bool is considered non-int for this task and should also raise TypeError.

acceptance_criteria: 11. to_roman returns a value of type str for all valid inputs.
12. to_roman raises ValueError for integer inputs outside 1..3999, including 0, -1, and 4000.
13. to_roman raises TypeError for non-integer inputs, including '5', 5.0, None, and [1].
14. The existing is_roman_numeral function continues to pass its current tests (test_true and test_false in tests/test_basic.py).
out_of_scope: The implementer must not modify the is_roman_numeral function.
The implementer must not modify the test files (tests/test_basic.py and tests/__init__.py).
The implementer must not change the public interface of the roman package (i.e., the exported names in roman/__init__.py).
The implementer must not add external dependencies.
